title: Projective matrix group and its finite flat special-linear central cover
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $r\geq2$. Write $\operatorname{GL}_{r,k}=\operatorname{Spec}k[x_{ij},\det(x)^{-1}]$ and $\operatorname{SL}_{r,k}=\operatorname{Spec}k[x_{ij}]/(\det(x)-1)$, with matrix multiplication and determinant as in [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant], where $1\leq i,j\leq r$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, sk-def-av-group-scheme]. The fpqc sheaf quotient of $\operatorname{GL}_{r,k}$ by the scalar subgroup $\mathbf G_m$ is represented by an affine group scheme $\operatorname{PGL}_{r,k}$; here the quotient sheaf is the sheafification of $T\mapsto\operatorname{GL}_{r,k}(T)/\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)^\times$ for the coverings of [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Here faithfully flat means flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and surjective, and an $F$-torsor means a faithfully flat map $T\to S$ with the isomorphism $T\times F\simeq T\times_S T$ induced by the action. The quotient map $\operatorname{GL}_{r,k}\to\operatorname{PGL}_{r,k}$ is a faithfully flat $\mathbf G_m$-torsor. Its restriction $q:\operatorname{SL}_{r,k}\to\operatorname{PGL}_{r,k}$ is finite locally free of rank $r$ (an affine map whose direct-image structure module is locally free of rank $r$) and surjective, with central kernel $\mu_r=\operatorname{Spec}k[t]/(t^r-1)$ acting by scalar matrices. In particular it is an fpqc covering, and $(g,z)\mapsto(g,gz)$ is an isomorphism $\operatorname{SL}_{r,k}\times_k\mu_r\simeq\operatorname{SL}_{r,k}\times_{\operatorname{PGL}_{r,k}}\operatorname{SL}_{r,k}$. Both $\operatorname{SL}_{r,k}$ and $\operatorname{PGL}_{r,k}$ are smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and geometrically connected (their base changes to algebraically closed fields are connected), and each has Krull dimension $r^2-1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. These descriptions commute with field extension, without assuming $r$ invertible in $k$.

source.place: Milne, Algebraic Groups (2022 corrected text), Example 5.49, printed p.111 (GL/Gm and SL/mu_r); Propositions 5.24--5.27, printed pp.104--105 (torsor), and Proposition 7.15, printed p.142 (finite flatness for finite kernel). Section 2.42, printed p.53, gives SL connectedness and the variety isomorphism SL times Gm to GL; Proposition 1.62(b), printed p.24, gives smoothness of a quotient, and Proposition 5.23, printed p.104, gives the dimensions. The finite flat mu_r torsor has rank r since k[t]/(t^r-1) is free of rank r. Local PDF WANTED; primary PDF read online.

proof.text: Use [def-sc-general-linear-group] for the displayed GL and SL group schemes, and [def-sc-gm-ga] for scalar units and roots of unity. Apply [lem-sfb-projective-frames-pgl] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $V=\mathcal O_S^r$: its $G$ is the determinant-nonzero open in projective matrix space, with the Zariski-local matrix-lift property and scalar equality criterion. Call it $P$. Put $R=k[x_{ij}]$, graded by degree one. The determinant is homogeneous of positive degree $r$, directly from its Leibniz formula. Thus $P=D_+(\det)\subset\operatorname{Proj}R$ is affine by [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open]. This constructs the required affine group scheme rather than taking a quotient of groups of rational points.

source.place: Example 5.49; determinant-open model supplied by the existing projective-frame lemma; Stacks Constructions 01MB, lemma-proj-scheme (standard homogeneous affine opens), with 01M7, lemma-proj-sheaves (their coordinate rings).

proof.text: On the projective chart indexed by an entry $(a,b)$, normalize that entry to $1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts] its intersection $U_{ab}$ with $P$ is $\operatorname{Spec}B_{ab}$, where $B_{ab}=k[y_{ij}:(i,j)\ne(a,b)][1/d]$, $A=(y_{ij})$, $y_{ab}=1$, and $d=\det A$. Its inverse image in GL consists of matrices $g=sA$, with $s=g_{ab}\in\mathbf G_m$; the inverse is $g\mapsto(g_{ab},g/g_{ab})$. Hence $\operatorname{GL}|_{U_{ab}}\simeq U_{ab}\times\mathbf G_m$. These opens cover $P$. Each projection is smooth, since $\mathbf G_{m,U}$ is the open $D(t)$ in $\mathbf A^1_U$; cite [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth] and [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition]. Smoothness is local on the source by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source], so GL to $P$ is smooth, and is flat by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. The sections $A$ prove surjectivity. It is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine]; over each affine target open its affine inverse image is therefore itself the single affine required by [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering].

source.place: Tag 01NG, lemma-standard-covering-projective-space; Morphisms 01VC, 01VA, 01V6, 01VF; Milne 5.24--5.27 for the torsor viewpoint.

proof.text: If two matrices $g,h$ have the same image in $P$, the scalar-equality clause of [lem-sfb-projective-frames-pgl] gives the unique unit $z$ with $h=gz$. Uniqueness also follows from the $(1,1)$ entry of $g^{-1}h=zI$. This formula and its inverse are regular on the charts of step 2 and agree on their overlaps, so $(g,z)\mapsto(g,gz)$ identifies $\operatorname{GL}\times\mathbf G_m$ with $\operatorname{GL}\times_P\operatorname{GL}$. The faithfully flat map of step 2 is therefore the claimed torsor. Moreover $h_P$ is an fpqc sheaf by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent]. A map from the presheaf GL/scalars to any fpqc sheaf extends to $h_P$ by choosing the local matrix lifts of step 2: two lifts differ by a scalar, so their images agree, and the sheaf axiom glues them uniquely. Conversely restriction along GL gives the original map. This is precisely the universal property of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], establishing the stated fpqc quotient, including for nonaffine test schemes.

source.place: Propositions 5.24--5.27, printed pp.104--105; Stacks Descent Tag 023Q, lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms; Sites 00WH (sheafification universal property).

proof.text: Restrict the quotient homomorphism to SL. Over $U_{ab}$ a lift has the form $g=tA$ by step 2; the condition $\det g=1$ reads $t^rd=1$. This follows by taking the factor $t$ out of each of the $r$ factors in every Leibniz monomial. Thus $q^{-1}(U_{ab})\simeq\operatorname{Spec}C_{ab}$ with $C_{ab}=B_{ab}[t]/(t^r-d^{-1})$. Explicitly the map sends $t$ to $g_{ab}$ and $y_{ij}$ to $g_{ij}/g_{ab}$, while its inverse sends $g_{ij}$ to $ty_{ij}$. The denominators exist because $t^{-1}=dt^{r-1}$ and because step 2 identifies this inverse image inside GL with $U_{ab}\times\mathbf G_m$. The two substitutions fix every generator, so they are inverse algebra maps, hence inverse scheme maps by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. These are identities over arbitrary $k$-algebras, including rings with nilpotents.

source.place: Example 5.49, printed p.111: determinant-root lifting; explicit normalized-entry coordinate calculation by Q67.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free], each $C_{ab}$ is free over $B_{ab}$ with basis $1,t,\ldots,t^{r-1}$. Consequently the affine map over this chart is finite, flat and finitely presented: finiteness uses the displayed basis, flatness uses [lem-sc-affine-standard-cover-finite-free-local-fp-flat] and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion], and finite presentation uses the single displayed monic relation. Its fibre over any field has the same $r$-element basis. Therefore it is finite locally free of degree $r$ in [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. The $U_{ab}$ form an open, hence etale, covering by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-free-degree-etale-descent] gives the global assertion. Apply [lem-pc-flf-properties] to obtain the direct-image module formulation in the item. For each point $u$ of $U_{ab}$, choose a root $α$ of $t^r-d(u)^{-1}$ in an algebraic closure $L$ of its residue field. It is nonzero, and evaluation $C_{ab}\to L$, $t\mapstoα$, has prime kernel contracting to the prime of $u$. Thus $q$ is surjective. Both its source and target are affine, so [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine] and [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering] show that this flat surjection is an fpqc covering. No separability of the polynomial is used.

source.place: Tag 02VO, lemma-descending-property-finite-locally-free, applied to the Zariski chart cover; Morphisms 02KB, lemma-finite-flat; Milne Example 5.49 and Proposition 7.15, printed pp.111,142--143.

proof.text: The GL torsor identity in step 3 identifies the kernel of $q$ with scalars $zI$ satisfying $z^r=1$, that is the full group scheme $\mu_r$ of [def-sc-gm-ga]. Scalar multiplication commutes with every matrix, so this kernel is central over every test algebra. For $g,h\in\operatorname{SL}(T)$ with equal images, the unique scalar $z$ of step 3 obeys $1=\det h=z^r\det g=z^r$. Hence the same inverse formula gives $(g,z)\mapsto(g,gz)$ and $ (g,h)\mapsto(g,g^{-1}h)$ as mutually inverse morphisms $\operatorname{SL}\times\mu_r\simeq\operatorname{SL}\times_P\operatorname{SL}$, where in the latter formula the scalar is read from the $(1,1)$ entry. This verifies the scheme-theoretic kernel and the fibre-product clause even when $\mu_r$ is nonreduced.

source.place: Example 5.49 and Proposition 5.24, printed pp.111,104; restricting the explicit GL torsor identity.

proof.text: Every chart $U_{ab}$ is an open of affine $(r^2-1)$-space, hence smooth by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth] and [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition]; their cover gives smoothness of $P$ by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source]. To check SL directly, write $c_{ij}$ for the signed cofactor of $x_{ij}$. Cofactor expansion, obtained by grouping the Leibniz sum by the value in row $i$, gives $\det X=c_{ij}x_{ij}+b$ with $c_{ij},b$ independent of $x_{ij}$. On $D(c_{ij})$ in SL, solving gives $x_{ij}=(1-b)/c_{ij}$, identifying that chart with $\operatorname{Spec}k[x_{uv}:(u,v)\ne(i,j)][1/c_{ij}]$. These opens cover SL: the identity $X\operatorname{adj}(X)=I$ of [lem-weil-pbc-matrix-adjugate-identity] shows that its cofactors generate the unit ideal when $\det X=1$. These are again opens of affine $(r^2-1)$-space, so the same smoothness lemmas apply. Finally SL is finite type from its finite polynomial quotient presentation; $P$ is finite type from its finite cover by the $U_{ab}$, each having finitely many generators and one inverted element, using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: Tags 01V6, 01VC, 01VA; standard affine-space smoothness 00T7; explicit cofactor charts, consistent with Milne Examples 2.40--2.42 and Corollary 5.26.

proof.text: Over any field extension $K/k$, the polynomial ring $K[x_{ij}]$ is a domain by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain], and $\det$ is nonzero since evaluation at the identity gives $1$. Its localization at $\det$ is a nonzero domain: by the fraction equivalence in [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property], $a/(\det)^m=0$ iff some nonzero power of $\det$ annihilates $a$, hence iff $a=0$. Thus a product of two nonzero fractions is nonzero, and $1/1\ne0$. Hence GL is integral; equivalently its zero prime has closure the whole spectrum by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes], so GL is irreducible. The regular map $g\mapsto g\operatorname{diag}(\det(g)^{-1},1,\ldots,1)$ to SL is surjective, having the inclusion of SL as a section. Thus SL is irreducible: a decomposition into two proper closed sets would pull back to such a decomposition of GL. The quotient map GL to $P$ is also surjective by step 2, so the same argument gives irreducibility of $P$. Both are nonempty (the identity). Irreducibility implies connectedness by [lem-pc-irreducible-space-connected]. Taking $K$ algebraically closed proves geometric connectedness. For use in the next step, SL is also integral: the maps $(h,u)\mapsto h\operatorname{diag}(u,1,\ldots,1)$ and $g\mapsto(g\operatorname{diag}(\det(g)^{-1},1,\ldots,1),\det(g))$ are inverse, write $N:\operatorname{GL}\to\operatorname{SL}$ for the normalization and $i:\operatorname{SL}\to\operatorname{GL}$ for inclusion. Since $N\circ i=\mathrm{id}$, the coordinate maps satisfy $i^*N^*=\mathrm{id}$. Thus $N^*:K[\operatorname{SL}]\hookrightarrow K[\operatorname{GL}]$ is injective, so its source is a nonzero domain. This also makes explicit the inclusion of Laurent constant polynomials under the displayed product isomorphism.

source.place: Examples 2.40 and 2.42, printed pp.52--53; explicit determinant-normalization isomorphism and elementary continuous-image argument.

proof.text: The nonempty chart $D(c_{11})$ in SL contains the identity and is the nonempty principal open of affine $(r^2-1)$-space described in step 7. Polynomial rings over $k$ have dimension $r^2-1$ by [lem-sf-noetherian-polynomial-dimension] (a field is Noetherian of dimension zero). Apply [lem-sc-integral-locally-algebraic-opens-dimension] first to this open in affine space and then to this open in the integral finite-type scheme SL: $\dim\operatorname{SL}=r^2-1$. For $P$, choose $U_{11}$, also containing the identity and a principal open of affine $(r^2-1)$-space. Its coordinate ring is a domain; since $P$ is irreducible by step 8 and covered by such reduced affine charts, it is integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. The same open-dimension lemma yields $\dim P=\dim U_{11}=r^2-1$. Ring and topological dimensions agree here because [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes] identifies strict chains of irreducible closed sets with the reversed strict chains of primes.

source.place: Tag 0A21, lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic, part (3); Algebra polynomial dimension, and Milne Proposition 5.23 as the matching quotient dimension formula.

proof.text: All the displayed equations, matrix multiplication, normalized-entry maps, cofactor substitutions and inverse formulas have coefficients in $k$ and remain the same after tensoring with any extension field $K$. The projective-frame node explicitly asserts arbitrary base-change compatibility for the determinant-open quotient. Affine fibre products are computed by tensor products by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]; hence the GL, SL and $\mu_r$ presentations become the corresponding presentations over $K$, and the morphism $q$, its kernel and the torsor isomorphisms are the same maps over $K$. The monic basis calculation remains valid over $K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free], while steps 7--9 apply to that field without additional hypotheses. This proves every stated field-extension compatibility. In characteristic $p$ dividing $r$, the relation $t^r-1$ may have repeated factors, but neither the rank calculation nor any chart argument divided by $r$.
